sources.note: Nothing; tertiary page used only to harvest the reference list (Singer 2007; Sasseville 2025a, 2025b).

sources.citation: Sasseville, David. 2025b. Appendix 2: The Language of KBo 19.164+. In F. Giusfredi, A. Matessi, S. Merlin & V. Pisaniello (eds.), Contacts of Languages and Peoples in the Hittite and Post-Hittite World, vol. 2, 389-390. Leiden: Brill. doi:10.1163/9789004729704_020 (CC BY-NC-ND; OAPEN copy).
sources.note: Nothing. Reports that KBo 19.164+ (four joined fragments from Hattuša) preserves a language argued to be Kaskean; 'the highly fragmentary context makes any attempt at translating in vain'; identifies affixes (-hši, -ruwi, -ēni, -itta, ma-, ha-, ta-, we-, pi-), full reduplication, and patronymic pi-/-ēni. No phonology, no accent.

sources.citation: Simon, Zsolt. 2025. Ch. 9 On the Fringes: Kartvelian, Armenian, Etruscan, and Lemnian. In Giusfredi et al. (eds.), Contacts of Languages and Peoples in the Hittite and Post-Hittite World, vol. 2, 198ff. Leiden: Brill.
sources.note: Nothing. p. 199: 'we know nothing about the Kaška language beyond onomastics, an in-depth investigation of which remains a desideratum (but see now Sasseville forthcoming..)'.

sources.citation: Singer, Itamar. 2007. Who were the Kaška? Phasis (Tbilisi) 10(II): 166-181.
sources.note: Nothing. p. 170: 'In view of the total absence of Kaškan written sources, the only type of evidence available to us are private names – place names, personal names and divine names'; pp. 170-171 note suffixes -ška, -ili, -alli and reduplicated names; p. 178 reports Giorgadze's Zan (Megrelian/Laz) hypothesis without endorsing it.

sources.citation: von Schuler, Einar. 1965. Die Kaškäer: Ein Beitrag zur Ethnographie des alten Kleinasiens (Untersuchungen zur Assyriologie und Vorderasiatischen Archäologie 3). Berlin: de Gruyter. xv+197 pp. Ch. IV 'Das sprachliche Material', pp. 83-107.
sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress (no hit for Akzent/Betonung in a linguistic sense). Ch. IV §1 p. 84 states that the material is names only and 'gestattet keine Aussagen über die Sprachstruktur und sprachliche Verwandtschaft des Kaškäischen'; §5 (pp. 100-107) lists sound alternations, formatives, reduplication and bases in North-Anatolian names; §2 pp. 86-88 discusses the vowel/sibilant of the name Kaška, not its accent.

sources.citation: Sasseville, David. 2025a. Kaskean: A New Recorded Language in the Archives of Ḫattuša? Altorientalische Forschungen 52(1): 70-92.
